title: Adjoining one left translated chart preserves strictness
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subset Y$ in an $S$-scheme is $S$-dense if $U_s$ is dense in $Y_s$ for every $s\in S$. An $S$-rational map is a morphism on an $S$-dense open, modulo agreement on an $S$-dense common open; an $S$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens. Smoothness and finite type have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A strict birational law on a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme $Y$ with nonempty fibres is an associative $S$-rational map $m:Y\times_SY\dashrightarrow Y$ for which there are opens $D,V,W\subset Y\times_SY$, each dense in every fibre of both projections to $Y$, such that $m$ is defined on $D$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$, $(x,y)\mapsto(m(x,y),y)$ induce isomorphisms $D\simeq V$ and $D\simeq W$, respectively. Let $Y\to S$ be smooth, separated, of finite type and have nonempty fibres, let $m$ be a strict birational law on $Y$, and let $a:S\to Y$ be a section. Put $\tau_a(y)=m(a,y)$ as an $S$-rational map. Let $T_a\subseteq Y\times_SY$ be the scheme-theoretic closure [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] of its graph, with projections $r_1,r_2:T_a\to Y$. Both projections are open immersions with $S$-dense images. Take a second copy $Y(a)$ of $Y$, with its copy isomorphism $c_a:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y(a)$, and glue $Y$ and $Y(a)$ by identifying $r_2(t)$ in the first copy with $c_a(r_1(t))$ in the second copy, for $t\in T_a$. There is a scheme $Y^+$ with open immersions $i:Y\hookrightarrow Y^+$ and $k:Y(a)\hookrightarrow Y^+$, whose images cover $Y^+$ and whose intersection is precisely this identified copy of $T_a$. The scheme $Y^+$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $S$ and has nonempty fibres; both charts are $S$-dense. There is a strict birational law $m^+$ on $Y^+$ restricting to $m$ on $Y$. As an $S$-rational map $Y\dashrightarrow Y^+$, $i\tau_a$ has the everywhere-defined representative $k c_a:Y\to Y^+$.

source.place: 5.3 construction before Lemma 5 and Lemma 5, printed pp.122-124 (PDF pp.128-130); primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-strict-law-graph-charts] for the graph closure $\Gamma$ and replace the original strictness domain by $D=q_{12}(\Gamma)$. Write $\Phi(x,y)=(x,m(x,y))$, $\Psi(x,y)=(m(x,y),y)$ and $V=\Phi(D)$, $W=\Psi(D)$. They are isomorphisms from $D$ to $V,W$, and all three opens are dense in every fibre of either projection. The base-change lemma makes this fibrewise density available after arbitrary residue-field extension. All finite products of $Y$ over $S$, and their opens, are reduced and locally Noetherian by the smooth reducedness lemma, and Noetherian by finite type over $S$. Consequently a dense open in any of these schemes is schematically dense: its inclusion is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so apply the reduced dense-image lemma. Equality on such an open into a separated target therefore gives equality of morphisms by the separated uniqueness lemma. We will use precisely this equality criterion below.

source.place: BLR 5.3 Lemma 3 and its paragraph on maximal domains; reduced-density preparation for the construction and Lemma 5

proof.text: Form $C_a=\Gamma\times_{Y,\,q_1,a}S$, regarded as a closed subscheme of $Y\times_SY$ by its second and third coordinates. Its two maps to $Y$ are the base changes of $q_{12}$ and $q_{13}$ along $y\mapsto(a,y)$; hence both are open immersions. The graph of $m(a,-)$ on the pullback of the original strictness domain is contained in $C_a$. Its first-coordinate image is $S$-dense in $Y$, so it is dense in the open first-coordinate image of $C_a$. This makes that graph schematically dense in $C_a$, which is reduced as an open of $Y$. Since $C_a$ is closed in $Y^2$, its schematic closure is exactly $T_a$. Thus $T_a=C_a$. Each projection has $S$-dense image because it is the base change along $a$ of the corresponding projection-dense graph chart. In particular this proves the assertions about $r_1,r_2$ without assuming that schematic closure commutes with arbitrary base change.

source.place: BLR 5.3 construction preceding Lemma 5, p.122; graph-closure slice justified using Lemma 3

proof.text: Set $O_2=r_2(T_a)\subset Y$ and $O_1=c_a r_1(T_a)\subset Y(a)$. The overlap isomorphism $O_2\to O_1$ is $c_a r_1 r_2^{-1}$, with inverse $r_2r_1^{-1}c_a^{-1}$. Use identity overlaps on each chart and these mutually inverse maps on the two mixed overlaps. The cocycle equations reduce to the two inverse identities. Apply the scheme-gluing lemma; it gives $P=Y^+$ and open immersions $i,k$ covering $P$, with intersection exactly $T_a$. The two structural maps to $S$ agree on $T_a$ since both $r_j$ are over $S$, and glue to $P\to S$. Put $h=kc_a:Y\to P$.

source.place: BLR 5.3 two-copy gluing construction, p.122; Stacks 01JB/01JC for the gluing and its intersections

proof.text: On the four open charts of $P\times_SP$, the inverse image of the diagonal of $P/S$ is respectively the diagonal of $Y/S$, the diagonal of $Y(a)/S$, and the two copies of $T_a$ with the coordinates interchanged as necessary. All are closed immersions: the first two by separatedness of $Y$, the others by the definition of $T_a$. Closedness of the image is local on this open cover, and surjectivity of the structure-sheaf map can be checked on the same cover. Thus the diagonal is a closed immersion, so $P/S$ is separated. Smoothness can be checked on the affine neighbourhoods already contained in the two charts, where the structural ring maps are exactly those of $Y/S$. The union of finite affine covers of the two charts is a finite affine cover of $P$ by finite-type $A$-algebras, proving finite type. Its fibres are nonempty since they contain the fibres of $Y$. In each fibre the overlap is dense in each chart, by step 2, so each whole chart is dense in $P_s$. Hence $i(Y)$ and $h(Y)$ are $S$-dense.

source.place: BLR 5.3 construction, p.122, separatedness and the two S-dense smooth finite-type charts

proof.text: For every $T\to S$, the base change of the $S$-dense chart $i(Y)$ is $T$-dense by the smooth density clause of the base-change lemma (the density clause requires only smoothness, not a strict law on $P$). It follows successively that $i(Y)^r$ is $S$-dense in $P^r$ for $r=2,3$. Define the rational law $m^+$ on $P$ by the morphism $i\circ m$ on the open $(i\times i)(D)$. This is a representative on an $S$-dense open. The rational identity $(xy)z=x(yz)$ holds on an $S$-dense open of $Y^3$, and hence of $P^3$: the needed successive product domains are dense because the original universal translations are projection-birational. Thus $m^+$ is associative and restricts to $m$. The universal rational translations of $m^+$ are birational since they coincide with those of $m$ on this common dense chart. The overlap equation $i r_2=h r_1$ also says $i\tau_a=h$ on the $S$-dense first image of $T_a$; hence $h$ is the required everywhere-defined representative.

source.place: BLR 5.3 p.123 before and at the beginning of Lemma 5: extension as a rational law and the extended left translation

proof.text: Here are explicit regular representatives on the opens used to establish strictness. Let $U_0=(i\times i)(D)$ with $\mu_0(i x,i y)=i(xy)$, and let $U_1=(h\times i)(D)$ with $\mu_1(hx,iy)=h(xy)$. Define the open $B_a=\{x:(x,a)\in D\}$ and its morphism $\beta:B_a\to Y$, $\beta(x)=m(x,a)$. It is an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens, as the base change of $\Psi:D\simeq W$ at the second coordinate $a$. Let $E_2=\{(x,y):x\in B_a,\ (\beta(x),y)\in D\}$, an open of $Y^2$, and put $U_2=(i\times h)(E_2)$ with $\mu_2(ix,hy)=i(\beta(x)y)$. These are morphisms. The formulas are the ordered expressions $xy$, $a(xy)$, and $(xa)y$; no commutativity is used.

source.place: BLR 5.3 Lemma 5(a), pp.123-124: the three multiplication opens and their formulas

proof.text: Let $A_a=r_1(T_a)$ and $\alpha:A_a\to r_2(T_a)$ be the open translation isomorphism. In $U_1$ restrict to the open where $x\in A_a$, $xy\in A_a$, and $(\alpha(x),y)\in D$. There $hx=i(ax)$ and associativity gives $h(xy)=i(a(xy))=i((ax)y)$. In $U_2$ restrict to the open where $y\in A_a$ and $(x,\alpha(y))\in D$; then $hy=i(ay)$ and $i((xa)y)=i(x(ay))$. These restrictions are dense: each is a finite intersection of translation domains and inverse images of dense opens under the birational maps supplied by graph-charts. This can be tested in each fibre after residue-field extension. Hence each $\mu_j$ represents $m^+$. On each $U_j\cap U_l$ the morphisms agree on a dense open. The overlap is reduced and Noetherian, while $P$ is separated by step 4, so schematic density and separated uniqueness give equality on the entire overlap. Morphism gluing gives $\mu:U'=U_0\cup U_1\cup U_2\to P$, a representative of $m^+$.

source.place: BLR 5.3 Lemma 5(a), agreement by associativity and gluing, pp.123-124

proof.text: The open $U_0\cup U_1$ is dense in every fibre of the first projection $P^2\to P$: for first coordinate $ix$ use the dense row of $D$ in $U_0$, and for $hx$ use that in $U_1$. The old second chart $i(Y)$ is itself universally fibre-dense in $P$, so either row is dense in the whole projection fibre. For the second projection, points in $i(Y)$ are handled by $U_0$. For a second coordinate $hy$ in the new chart, the allowed first coordinates in $U_2$ are $x\in B_a$ with $(\beta(x),y)\in D$. The second condition cuts out a dense open in $Y$ as $\beta(x)$ varies; its intersection with the dense image of $\beta$ is dense, and its inverse image under the open isomorphism $\beta$ is dense in $Y$. Thus this fibre is dense too. These arguments apply over the residue field of each point, using the residue-field extension clause in graph-charts and universal density. This proves that $U'$ is dense in every fibre of both projections.

source.place: BLR 5.3 Lemma 5(a), projection-density of U union U1 union U2

proof.text: Let $F=(p_1,\mu)$ and $H=(\mu,p_2)$ on $U'$. On $U_0$ these are $\Phi,\Psi$ in the old charts. On $U_1$, the formulas are $(hx,iy)\mapsto(hx,h(xy))$ and $(hx,iy)\mapsto(h(xy),iy)$, so they are $\Phi,\Psi$ conjugated by chart isomorphisms. On $U_2$, use coordinates $u=\beta(x)$ on $B_a$. The map $F$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,uy)$ followed by $i\times i$; this is the base change of the first-coordinate-preserving open immersion $\Phi$ along $\beta$ in the first coordinate. The map $H$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(uy,hy)$, obtained by $\beta\times\mathrm{id}$ on the source, $\Psi$ on its open domain, and $i\times h$ on the target. Thus both $F$ and $H$ are open immersions on each $U_j$.

source.place: BLR 5.3 Lemma 5(b), local universal-translation formulas, p.124

proof.text: For completeness, the local inverses from step 9 glue, so no birational form of Zariski Main is left implicit here. Do this for $F$ (the argument for $H$ is identical). On $F(U_j)\cap F(U_l)$, the images of $U_j\cap U_0$ and $U_l\cap U_0$ are dense opens: $U_0$ is dense in $U'$, and both restrictions of $F$ are open isomorphisms. Their intersection is dense, and there the inverse branches coincide since $F|_{U_0}=\Phi$ is injective. The intersection of target images is reduced and Noetherian; the inverse branches into the separated scheme $P^2$ therefore agree everywhere by the schematic-density and separated uniqueness lemmas. Glue the inverse branches on the union of the target images. They are two-sided inverses to $F$ by checking on the $U_j$. Hence $F$ is an isomorphism onto its open image $V'$. Applying the same argument to $H$ gives an isomorphism $U'\simeq W'=H(U')$.

source.place: BLR 5.3 Lemma 5(b), global open-immersion conclusion, with the elementary inverse-gluing argument replacing its Zariski Main invocation

proof.text: The open $V'$ contains $(i\times i)(V)$ from $U_0$ and $(h\times h)(V)$ from $U_1$. Each copy of $V$ is dense in every fibre of either projection within its two charts. For a first coordinate in $i(Y)$ use the first copy, and for a first coordinate in $h(Y)$ use the second; the remaining chart in that fibre is dense in the whole fibre. This proves first-projection density of $V'$. For a second coordinate in either chart use the same two copies with the roles of the coordinates interchanged. Universal density of the charts and the residue-field extension clause in graph-charts justify this for every scheme point. Thus $V'$ is dense in every fibre of both projections.

source.place: BLR 5.3 Lemma 5(b), V contains V union V1, p.124

proof.text: For $W'$, the copies $(i\times i)(W)\subset H(U_0)$ and $(h\times i)(W)\subset H(U_1)$ prove density in fibres of the first projection, for first coordinates in either chart. They also prove density in fibres of the second projection at points in $i(Y)$. For a second coordinate $hy$ in $h(Y)$, use $H(U_2)$: its first coordinates are $i(\beta(x)y)$. The map $x\mapsto\beta(x)y$ is the composite of the birational right translation $\beta:x\mapsto xa$ with the birational right translation $u\mapsto uy$. It is defined on exactly the open used in $E_2$ over $y$ and has dense open image in $Y$; intersections of the two domain/image opens remain dense. This uses only the graph-chart fibrewise birationality, after extension to $\kappa(y)$. The image is dense in the whole first-coordinate fibre of $P$ since $i(Y)$ is universally dense. Therefore $W'$ is dense in every fibre of both projections.

source.place: BLR 5.3 Lemma 5(b), W2 and right-translation argument for the second projection, p.124

proof.text: Steps 8, 10, 11 and 12 exhibit the opens $U',V',W'\subset P^2$, each dense in every fibre of either projection, with $\mu$ regular on $U'$ and universal translations giving isomorphisms $U'\simeq V'$ and $U'\simeq W'$. Together with associativity from step 5 this is precisely a strict birational law on $P$. The chart properties and the everywhere-defined representative $h=kc_a$ were proved in steps 3-5, giving every asserted clause.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q27-90ad5a8e2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's statement and all 13 steps in full, along with the statement of every cited node (graph-charts, strict-law base-change, trf smooth-reduced-dense-pullback, pbc finite-type-over-noetherian/open-immersion-base-change/glue-schemes/morphism-gluing, nagata reduced-dense-image and separated-equality). BLR §5.3 Lemma 5 is not in literature/, so proof_origin=agent with a WANTED line is correct, and I checked the mathematics independently. Step 2: C_a = Γ×_{Y,q1,a}S is closed in Y², and its maps to Y are base changes of q12/q13, so they are open immersions. D_a is S-dense because a(s) is a rational point, so the graph is schematically dense and T_a = C_a. Step 4: the diagonal on the four chart products is Δ_Y, Δ_{Y(a)} and two swapped copies of T_a, all closed. Step 5: h = kc_a agrees with iτ_a on r1(T_a) because ir2 = hr1, so the orientation is right. Steps 6–7: β is the base change of Ψ at y=a, the ordered formulas (ax)y = a(xy) and (xa)y = x(ay) are correct, and the extra domain conditions are dense preimages. Steps 9–10: F and H are explicit composites of Φ/Ψ/β with chart maps; the inverse branches agree on a dense open because Φ is a monomorphism, so they glue (this is genuinely elementary). Steps 8, 11, 12: I checked fibrewise density for both charts and both projections. Small cases: A^1∖{0} with addition and a=1 gives P = A^1 and h(y) = y+1; a group Y collapses to Y. There is no cycle, no duplicate in the strict-law family and no new nodes; this is not a re-split item.
